subject.title: Android node notification forwarding causes cross-session replies (WhatsApp duplicate sends to wrong group)

question: Should OpenClaw enforce this primarily as outbound session/channel binding, Android native-package notification suppression, Gateway notification package filtering, or a layered combination?
rationale: The remaining path crosses Android notification policy, Gateway node-session events, and heartbeat/message delivery authority, so automation should not choose the permanent security boundary or new default/config behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Harden outbound binding first
options.body: Reject or constrain cross-channel sends from node notification or heartbeat sessions unless a verified source route binding exists, then use Android or Gateway filtering as defense in depth.

options.title: Suppress native packages in Android
options.body: Default-block known native-channel package IDs in the Android app, reducing duplicate inputs but requiring maintained package ownership policy and upgrade proof.

options.title: Add Gateway package filtering
options.body: Reject or filter notification packages server-side, which gives operators a central control but adds config/default surface and does not alone settle outbound authority.

recommendation.title: Harden outbound binding first
recommendation.body: Reject or constrain cross-channel sends from node notification or heartbeat sessions unless a verified source route binding exists, then use Android or Gateway filtering as defense in depth.

likelyOwner.reason: The original feature history ties this person to both the Android notification event source and Gateway `notifications.changed` handling that need boundary direction.
